item.aggregated_output:
# MCP Kart

A local experiment in autonomous kart racing: can low-latency decision models drive a kart in real time through MCP?

Python physics runs continuously at 60 Hz in a separate worker process, independent of the HTTP/MCP event loop. Models select one of 15 steering/throttle/brake combinations through OpenRouter's Decisions API, and a driver submits those controls to a real MCP server. A browser spectator shows the live race and saved replays. After three continuous seconds off-road, a rescue returns the kart near its departure point, stopped and facing along the road. Rescues are counted; the race clock keeps running.

## Run locally

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), then:

```sh
uv sync
uv run mcpkart-web
```

Open [the spectator](http://127.0.0.1:8765/). The MCP endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`. Put your own `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the ignored `.env` file when running paid model experiments; see `.env.example`. The server and scripted reference do not require an API key.

In a second terminal, establish the offline reference and drive it through MCP:

```sh
uv run mcpkart-bench reference
uv run mcpkart-bench live-reference --output artifacts/live-reference
```

The viewer's archive selector and replay controls can play saved trials without changing a live race. Replay recordings, request evidence, routes, and the budget ledger live under the ignored `artifacts/` directory.

## Model experiments

```sh
uv run mcpkart-bench latency --samples 20 --output artifacts/latency
uv run mcpkart-bench screen --output artifacts/comparison
uv run mcpkart-bench compare --trials 10 --output artifacts/comparison
uv run python -m mcpkart.probe --output artifacts/telemetry-probes
uv run mcpkart-bench screen --telemetry road_physics --output artifacts/road-physics-screen
```

The initial PoC now focuses on **TypeSafe Jev 1.14**, and benchmark/probe commands default to Jev. Paid driving commands default to the `road_physics` observation profile; the scripted reference uses raw telemetry. Earlier OpenAI GPT-6 Luna Decisions and Cloudflare Clef recordings are preserved; those routes can be selected explicitly later with `--models`. A Jev pass will not count as validation of other models. Provider routes are saved before trials; automatic retries and fallbacks are disabled. Requests include coordinate conventions, handling limits, the selected kart/track telemetry, rescue state, and the next required checkpoint's geometry. No recommended controls or computed racing line are sent to a model.

`--telemetry` selects an observation profile. Original road/physics profiles and the newer compact and road-compass variants remain available; see `mcpkart-bench screen --help`. Physics profiles report cornering grip demand; compact profiles separate current pose from future bends. The [telemetry experiment](docs/experiments/0002-track-telemetry.md) and [Jev navigation iteration](docs/experiments/0003-jev-navigation.md) record comparisons and limits. Saved trial labels identify the profile; older recordings show that it was not recorded.

Probes accept `--repeats` and `--fixtures` for repeated focused comparisons. `--control-language explicit` names the same physical wheel/pedal inputs in words. `--instruction-style` can test a next-input question or general driving guide separately; the default preserves the original instructions. These options affect model evidence and instructions, without adding a steering controller.

The [gate and history experiment](docs/experiments/0004-gates-and-observation-history.md) adds opt-in `road_navigation`, `compact_navigation` and `road_history` profiles. Navigation profiles distinguish the bearing toward a gate from its crossing-plane orientation and explain finite forward gate credit. History uses at most three actual preceding driver observations within one second, clearing motion samples after rescue while retaining the observed checkpoint-progress clock. Use `--navigation-record` with the probe command to reconstruct valid off-axis and missed-gate cases from a saved trial.

Use `--reset-after-seconds X` on reference and model commands to change the rescue timeout; `0` disables it. Keep the same setting for paired references and model runs, and use a new output directory when changing experiment configuration. Commands based on observations captured before a rescue are discarded, then the driver gets a fresh observation.

The persistent `artifacts/budget.json` ledger enforces a $10 total cap and conservative reservations across reruns. Keep the ledger: deleting it would discard the spending history. A saved comparison refuses to resume if the implementation, simulation/rescue settings, paired baseline, pinned route or prompt configuration changes. Live reports retain the exact instructions and control descriptions. A comparison also verifies that the reference uses the same track and handling.

The current assisted experiment targets at least eight of ten three-lap runs, with median completed-run duration within twice the paired scripted reference. Reports distinguish total completions, completions without rescue, and rescue counts. Assisted completion does not establish the original unassisted-driving goal. Incomplete batches never count as passes. This experiment compares complete model/provider routes and driver observations; it does not isolate model compute latency or establish general model rankings.

Saved replay bodies are prepared before the race clock starts and remain playable during a live trial. Newly saved recordings appear between races. Downloading the current trial is available after it ends, keeping large JSON work outside the physics clock.

Trial timing includes bounded GC, slow-span and late-wake CPU diagnostics. `uv run mcpkart-web --watchdog` additionally enables a small diagnostic thread in the physics worker that records source-only event-loop stacks during long physics gaps; locals are never captured. Full bounded evidence is saved in recordings, while the live viewer receives summaries. Instrumentation does not change physics, timing limits or GC policy. The [gate/history experiment](docs/experiments/0004-gates-and-observation-history.md) records earlier timing failures. All three initial controls in the [process isolation experiment](docs/experiments/0005-isolated-physics-clock.md) passed, including an HTTP-parent pause. A Jev screen also had valid timing but reached only 63/120 gates. Later model-free diagnostics and a native sleeper control reproduced intermittent failures, so local paid testing is held again. Process-isolated asyncio pacing remains the default; `--clock-pacing native` retains the unqualified native sleeper experiment, and `--clock-backend event_loop` selects the earlier combined runtime. Reports retain runtime identity and worker provenance; interrupted collection preserves request evidence as an incomplete trial.

## Development

For Linux, the [Docker/container guide](docs/linux-container.md) builds the same
locked Python environment and publishes a separate spectator on port 8766.
The first [Linux timing control](docs/experiments/0006-linux-docker-clock.md)
completed three laps but exceeded the 100 ms maximum-lateness limit at
104.26 ms. Jev remained held; Docker on this Mac has not established reliable timing.

An optional [Rust race-worker spike](docs/experiments/0007-rust-race-engine.md)
keeps Python/FastMCP and the existing physics contract. Build it with
`cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path rust-race/Cargo.toml`, then
start `uv run mcpkart-web --race-engine rust --port 8767`. The Docker image also
includes the release binary. Parity passes, but control two exceeded the
timing limit at 117.09 ms; Rust is experimental and local paid tests remain held.

The [GCP follow-up](docs/experiments/0008-remote-linux-clock.md) passed all three
Rust controls and the 170.1 s check, with at most 0.86 ms lateness. A subsequent
Jev screen had valid timing (1.20 ms maximum), but reached only 50/120 gates
with 24 rescues. The temporary VM was deleted after collection. Local timing
remains unqualified.

The [Python-on-GCP comparison](docs/experiments/0009-python-on-gcp.md) then passed
the same three races and 170.1 s check using the existing isolated Python
worker with asyncio pacing. Worst race lateness was 2.22 ms; the long check
peaked at 3.28 ms with 1.30 ms p95. All races finished without rescues, and
independent replay passed. **Keep Python for the current solo PoC**; Rust's
lower jitter is not required for this workload. The temporary VM and boot disk
were deleted. Further Jev experiments can use the qualified GCP environment;
multiplayer capacity and Temporal integration remain to be measured.

```sh
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check src tests scripts
```

The [approved experiment](docs/experiments/0001-realtime-driving.md), [broader project plan](docs/plan.md), [API research](docs/research/decision-models.md), and [glossary](GLOSSARY.md) record the design. Temporal orchestration, multiplayer collisions, items, authentication, and matchmaking follow the solo-driving evidence.

The previous implementation and documentation are preserved in [`legacy/`](legacy/README.md). Run that project's documented commands from `legacy/`.

A local experiment in autonomous kart racing: can low-latency decision models drive a kart in real time through MCP?

Python physics runs continuously at 60 Hz in a separate worker process, independent of the HTTP/MCP event loop. Models select one of 15 steering/throttle/brake combinations through OpenRouter's Decisions API, and a driver submits those controls to a real MCP server. A browser spectator shows the live race and saved replays. After three continuous seconds off-road, a rescue returns the kart near its departure point, stopped and facing along the road. Rescues are counted; the race clock keeps running.

## Run locally

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), then:

```sh
uv sync
uv run mcpkart-web
```

Open [the spectator](http://127.0.0.1:8765/). The MCP endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`. Put your own `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the ignored `.env` file when running paid model experiments; see `.env.example`. The server and scripted reference do not require an API key.

In a second terminal, establish the offline reference and drive it through MCP:

```sh
uv run mcpkart-bench reference
uv run mcpkart-bench live-reference --output artifacts/live-reference
```

The viewer's archive selector and replay controls can play saved trials without changing a live race. Replay recordings, request evidence, routes, and the budget ledger live under the ignored `artifacts/` directory.

## Model experiments

```sh
uv run mcpkart-bench latency --samples 20 --output artifacts/latency
uv run mcpkart-bench screen --output artifacts/comparison
uv run mcpkart-bench compare --trials 10 --output artifacts/comparison
uv run python -m mcpkart.probe --output artifacts/telemetry-probes
uv run mcpkart-bench screen --telemetry road_physics --output artifacts/road-physics-screen
```

The initial PoC now focuses on **TypeSafe Jev 1.14**, and benchmark/probe commands default to Jev. Paid driving commands default to the `road_physics` observation profile; the scripted reference uses raw telemetry. Earlier OpenAI GPT-6 Luna Decisions and Cloudflare Clef recordings are preserved; those routes can be selected explicitly later with `--models`. A Jev pass will not count as validation of other models. Provider routes are saved before trials; automatic retries and fallbacks are disabled. Requests include coordinate conventions, handling limits, the selected kart/track telemetry, rescue state, and the next required checkpoint's geometry. No recommended controls or computed racing line are sent to a model.

`--telemetry` selects an observation profile. Original road/physics profiles and the newer compact and road-compass variants remain available; see `mcpkart-bench screen --help`. Physics profiles report cornering grip demand; compact profiles separate current pose from future bends. The [telemetry experiment](docs/experiments/0002-track-telemetry.md) and [Jev navigation iteration](docs/experiments/0003-jev-navigation.md) record comparisons and limits. Saved trial labels identify the profile; older recordings show that it was not recorded.

Probes accept `--repeats` and `--fixtures` for repeated focused comparisons. `--control-language explicit` names the same physical wheel/pedal inputs in words. `--instruction-style` can test a next-input question or general driving guide separately; the default preserves the original instructions. These options affect model evidence and instructions, without adding a steering controller.

The [gate and history experiment](docs/experiments/0004-gates-and-observation-history.md) adds opt-in `road_navigation`, `compact_navigation` and `road_history` profiles. Navigation profiles distinguish the bearing toward a gate from its crossing-plane orientation and explain finite forward gate credit. History uses at most three actual preceding driver observations within one second, clearing motion samples after rescue while retaining the observed checkpoint-progress clock. Use `--navigation-record` with the probe command to reconstruct valid off-axis and missed-gate cases from a saved trial.

Use `--reset-after-seconds X` on reference and model commands to change the rescue timeout; `0` disables it. Keep the same setting for paired references and model runs, and use a new output directory when changing experiment configuration. Commands based on observations captured before a rescue are discarded, then the driver gets a fresh observation.

The persistent `artifacts/budget.json` ledger enforces a $10 total cap and conservative reservations across reruns. Keep the ledger: deleting it would discard the spending history. A saved comparison refuses to resume if the implementation, simulation/rescue settings, paired baseline, pinned route or prompt configuration changes. Live reports retain the exact instructions and control descriptions. A comparison also verifies that the reference uses the same track and handling.

The current assisted experiment targets at least eight of ten three-lap runs, with median completed-run duration within twice the paired scripted reference. Reports distinguish total completions, completions without rescue, and rescue counts. Assisted completion does not establish the original unassisted-driving goal. Incomplete batches never count as passes. This experiment compares complete model/provider routes and driver observations; it does not isolate model compute latency or establish general model rankings.

Saved replay bodies are prepared before the race clock starts and remain playable during a live trial. Newly saved recordings appear between races. Downloading the current trial is available after it ends, keeping large JSON work outside the physics clock.

Trial timing includes bounded GC, slow-span and late-wake CPU diagnostics. `uv run mcpkart-web --watchdog` additionally enables a small diagnostic thread in the physics worker that records source-only event-loop stacks during long physics gaps; locals are never captured. Full bounded evidence is saved in recordings, while the live viewer receives summaries. Instrumentation does not change physics, timing limits or GC policy. }
CLOCK_MODES = {"rust": "rust_fixed_step_wall_clock", "python": "fixed_step_wall_clock"}


def transform_helper(content: bytes, destination: str, engine: str,
                     artifact_directory: str | None = None) -> tuple[bytes, list[dict]]:
    """Adapt only artifact paths, labels, and runtime identity in frozen helpers."""

    def replace(old: bytes, new: bytes, count: int) -> None:
        nonlocal content

                b"info['clock_mode'] == '" + mode.encode() + b"' and " + identity, 1)
        if engine == "python":
            replace(b"Rust", b"Python", 2)
    elif destination.endswith("environment.py"):
        replace(b"assert info['process_pid'] > 1 and info['clock_mode'] == 'rust_fixed_step_wall_clock'",
                b"assert info['process_pid'] > 1 and info['backend'] == 'process' and "

    return content, substitutions


def prepare_validation(root: Path, output: Path, engine: str = "python") -> dict:
    """Materialize only the frozen free controls beside their future results.

# Codex Cloud development

Use the process-isolated Python engine with asyncio pacing for the current
solo PoC. The [GCP comparison](experiments/0009-python-on-gcp.md) passed the
timing gate with Python. That result does not qualify another machine: run
the free clock controls in the new Codex Cloud environment before buying more
Jev decisions. The local stalls do not establish a specific hardware cause.

## Prepare the environment

Create an environment for this repository's `main` branch, then ask its setup
conversation to run the following from the repository root:

```sh
bash scripts/setup_cloud.sh
.venv/bin/pytest -q
.venv/bin/ruff check src tests scripts
```

The script uses uv 0.12.23, selects Python 3.14.8, and installs the runtime and
development dependencies from `uv.lock` with `--locked`. It seeds a missing
ignored spending ledger from the recorded snapshot and preserves an existing
ledger. If the pinned uv is
missing, it installs to a versioned user directory without changing shell
profiles or replacing another uv installation. It starts no server, race,
Docker container, VM, or model request. Normal Python development needs no
Rust compiler or Docker. Tests that execute the optional Rust worker skip
when its release binary is absent.

In the current Cloud environment setup, save
`bash scripts/setup_cloud.sh` as the **Install script**. Configure a **Start
skill** to start services only when a task needs them, using the server command
below. Review the setup report and publish the environment. New tasks use the
published filesystem; republish dependency changes before starting a fresh
task. A script in this repository is a command to configure, not an
automatically discovered Codex environment configuration.
[Official OpenAI documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments#customize-installation-and-startup)
describes installation, startup, and saved state.

Enable the environment's **Package managers** network preset. If uv must be
bootstrapped, also allow `astral.sh`; its installer and managed Python downloads
use the GitHub release hosts included in that preset. PyPI dependencies need
`pypi.org` and `files.pythonhosted.org`, also included. Keep the environment's
proxy and certificate configuration in place for dependency and API requests.
See [Cloud networking](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments#connect-to-services)
and the [uv installer](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/installer/).

## Start the Python server

Run commands from the repository root. Use the installed interpreter directly
after setup so a timed experiment cannot trigger dependency installation.

```sh
env -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY .venv/bin/python -m mcpkart.web \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765 \
  --race-engine python --clock-backend process --clock-pacing asyncio
```

The MCP endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`; the spectator and JSON state
are `/` and `/api/state` on the same host. Run server and controller in the
same Cloud environment, with the same monotonic clock and process namespace.
The localhost URL belongs to that environment, not your Mac. Use any preview
or forwarding capability the environment actually provides; save recordings
for local replay if a browser preview is unavailable.

In a second terminal, generate a paired seed-zero reference and run one free
MCP smoke test:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m mcpkart.bench reference \
  --seeds 1 --delays 0 --output artifacts/cloud-reference.json
.venv/bin/python -m mcpkart.bench live-reference \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp \
  --reference artifacts/cloud-reference.json \
  --output artifacts/cloud-smoke-v1
```

The frozen handling and rescue settings should retain the 56.7-second offline
reference. Preserve a new output directory for each attempt. A single smoke
test is not the full timing gate.

## Qualify the clock before paid trials

Prepare the versioned seed-zero reference and helpers, then run the three
consecutive controls and long neutral check. These use the same frozen
protocol as the GCP comparison, without requiring Docker or GCP credentials.
Use a fresh directory for each attempt.

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/package_remote_clock.py \
  --engine python --prepare-directory artifacts/cloud-clock-v1
.venv/bin/python artifacts/cloud-clock-v1/run_controls.py && \
  .venv/bin/python artifacts/cloud-clock-v1/long_clock.py
```

Keep the server on port 8765 in the same environment. The control helper
reads `/api/state`, requires the Python process backend with
`fixed_step_wall_clock` and watchdog disabled, and checks the HTTP parent's
identity before pausing it. It resumes the parent during cleanup. Do not
substitute another environment's PID or the physics worker's PID.

All three must complete 120 gates with maximum lateness at most 100 ms,
exact final p95 at most 25 ms, and absolute final drift at most 100 ms. Race
two must record at least twelve physics samples during the HTTP-parent pause.
Stop at the first failure and preserve it; investigate the cause before a
new declared attempt. The `&&` runs the 170.1-second free neutral clock check
only after all three pass. Both stages include spectator polling. Review
`controls/validation.json`, the individual recordings, `long-clock.json`,
and `HELPER-MANIFEST.json` in the prepared directory before any paid screen.
See the [declared GCP protocol](experiments/0009-python-on-gcp.md).

Do builds, tests, source changes, and heavy analysis between timed runs. Keep
the server free of model credentials. Record the actual Cloud VM resources,
Python version, source fingerprint, runtime identity, timing evidence, and
results; the GCP result alone does not establish Cloud timing.

## Optional OpenRouter access

Model-free setup and controls do not require an API key. Add API access only
when the timing gate passes and the spending ledger is ready for migration.

In the current Cloud environment, configure `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` as a
**Network secret** with `openrouter.ai` as its allowed domain, and allow
HTTPS access to that host. Do not configure the same key as both a direct
environment variable and a network secret. Programs receive a placeholder;
the managed proxy replaces it in HTTPS requests to the allowed service,
during both setup and task execution. This project's HTTP client reads
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from its environment and uses the configured proxy.
Use the Personal vault if the value should belong to your account rather
than the shared environment.
[Official secret guidance](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments#configure-environment-variables-and-network-secrets)
explains these choices.

If your account instead shows **Codex Cloud (Legacy)**, its **Secrets** are
available only during setup and removed before the agent phase. A setup-only
secret therefore cannot directly supply a later paid driver. Use the access
mechanism supported by that environment and verify availability without
printing the key. Do not write a secret into a prepared image or commit it to
the repository to bridge those phases. See the
[legacy secret lifecycle](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment#environment-variables-and-secrets).

`artifacts/`, including the cumulative spending ledger and recordings, is
ignored by Git. Setup initializes a missing `artifacts/budget.json` from the
versioned [October 18 spending snapshot](experiments/model-budget-snapshot.json),
which records $0.914245672 charged against the $10 cap. It never overwrites an
existing ledger. This snapshot does not synchronize balances across machines:
copy the latest ledger when switching environments after further paid work,
and run only one paid experiment at a time. Do not reset the ledger or start
parallel paid writers with separate balances. Keep `.env` and raw credentials
out of commits, setup logs, and saved recordings.
These are the frozen inputs for `scripts/package_remote_clock.py`. They make the
credential-free Linux clock experiment reproducible from a fresh checkout,
without downloading the ignored local experiment artifacts.

`PROVENANCE.json` records their origin and hashes. The three `.py.in` helpers are
byte-for-byte copies of the historical Rust spike helpers. Their old artifact
paths and Rust identity checks are intentional templates: the packager replaces
only the declared paths, labels, and runtime identity for the selected engine,
and records every substitution in the package manifest.

`reference.json` retains the original reference metadata and its unchanged
successful seed-zero, zero-delay trial (56.7 seconds), including the exact track
and handling contract. Other calibration trials were omitted. It contains no
credentials or machine-specific environment facts. New model comparisons
should generate their own multi-seed reference as described in the root README.

Package an experiment locally (this makes no network or model calls):

```sh
uv run python scripts/package_remote_clock.py --engine python --output /tmp/python-clock.tar.gz
```

Run the resulting package on an existing Linux Docker host with
`bash scripts/run_remote_clock.sh --engine python /path/to/fresh/results`.
The runner builds and validates both engines for the historical parity check;
its timed races use only the selected engine. It does not provision a VM or run
paid model trials. The original local recordings remain under ignored
`artifacts/` paths.

To check an existing Linux server directly, prepare the helpers and run them
from the repository root, in the same PID namespace as the server:

```sh
uv run python scripts/package_remote_clock.py --engine python --prepare-directory artifacts/clock-check
uv run python artifacts/clock-check/run_controls.py
uv run python artifacts/clock-check/long_clock.py
```

The server must listen on `127.0.0.1:8765`, use the process backend with asyncio
pacing, and have the watchdog disabled. The control helper discovers and verifies
its parent PID before pausing it. Stop if either helper fails; preserve the
directory and use a new output path for another declared attempt.

"""Verify saved free-clock gates and final worker identity without starting work."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path

from mcpkart.bench import fingerprint

CLOCK_MODES = {"python": "fixed_step_wall_clock", "rust": "rust_fixed_step_wall_clock"}
LIMITS = {"max_lateness": 100, "p95_lateness": 25, "absolute_drift": 100}


def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def verify_race(race: dict, expected_info: dict, engine: str, label: str) -> None:
    mode = CLOCK_MODES[engine]
    module = "mcpkart.physics_worker" if engine == "python" else "mcpkart-rust-worker"
    for info in (expected_info, race["runtime_info"]):
        require(info["backend"] == "process" and info.get("engine", "python") == engine,
                f"{label}: wrong engine/backend")
        require(info["clock_mode"] == mode and info["physics_hz"] == 60,
                f"{label}: wrong clock mode/frequency")
        require(info["watchdog_enabled"] is False, f"{label}: watchdog enabled")
        require(info["process_pid"] == expected_info["process_pid"] > 1,
                f"{label}: HTTP parent identity changed")
    provenance, timing = race["process_provenance"], race["timing"]
    require(provenance["worker_module"] == module and provenance["child_clock_mode"] == mode,
            f"{label}: wrong final worker provenance")
    require(provenance["child_web_modules_loaded"] == [], f"{label}: web modules in physics child")
    require(provenance["parent_pid"] == expected_info["process_pid"]
            and provenance["child_pid"] > 1 and provenance["child_pid"] != provenance["parent_pid"],
            f"{label}: physics did not run in a distinct child")
    require(timing["process_provenance"] == provenance, f"{label}: timing provenance mismatch")
    require(timing["clock_mode"] == mode and timing["backend"] == "process"
            and timing["physics_hz"] == 60, f"{label}: wrong final timing clock")
    require(timing["validity_limits_ms"] == LIMITS, f"{label}: timing limits changed")
    require(timing["infrastructure_valid"] and race["realtime_valid"], f"{label}: timing gate failed")
    for key, limit in (("max_lateness_ms", 100), ("p95_lateness_ms", 25), ("drift_ms", 100)):
        require(math.isfinite(timing[key]) and abs(timing[key]) <= limit,
                f"{label}: {key} exceeds timing limit")


def verify(directory: Path, engine: str = "python") -> dict:
    require(engine in CLOCK_MODES, "Unknown engine")
    controls = json.loads((directory / "controls/validation.json").read_text())
    require(controls["passes"] and controls["source_unchanged"] and controls["model_requests"] == 0,
            "Scripted controls did not pass")
    require(len(controls["controls"]) == controls["required_consecutive_controls"] == 3,
            "Exactly three consecutive controls are required")
    require(controls["expected_clock_mode"] == CLOCK_MODES[engine], "Control clock mode changed")
    require(controls["validity_limits_ms"] == LIMITS, "Control timing limits changed")
    source = fingerprint()
    for index, row in enumerate(controls["controls"], 1):
        label = f"Control {index}"
        trial = json.loads((directory / f"controls/run-{index:02d}/scripted-live.json").read_text())
        race = trial["race"]
        require(row["passes"] and row["spectator_polls"] > 0, f"{label}: control gate failed")
        require(trial["fingerprint"] == row["fingerprint"] == source, f"{label}: source changed")
        require(not trial["runtime_mismatches"] and trial["collection_complete"],
                f"{label}: recording incomplete or runtime changed")
        require(race["summary"]["finished"] and race["summary"]["checkpoints_passed"] == 120,
                f"{label}: three-lap race did not finish")
        verify_race(race, controls["runtime_info"], engine, label)
        if index == 2:
            pause = row["parent_pause"]
            require(pause["race_id"] == race["race_id"]
                    and pause["parent_pid"] == controls["runtime_info"]["process_pid"],
                    "Parent pause targeted the wrong race or process")
            require(pause["signals"] == ["SIGSTOP", "SIGCONT"]
                    and abs(pause["requested_duration_s"] - .35) < 1e-6,
                    "Declared parent pause changed")
            samples = [sample for sample in race["samples"]
                       if pause["started_ns"] <= sample["wall_ns"] <= pause["ended_ns"]]
            require(len(samples) == pause["physics_samples_during_parent_pause"] >= 12,
                    "Insufficient actual child samples during parent pause")
    long = json.loads((directory / "long-clock.json").read_text())
    require(long["passes"] and long["model_requests"] == 0 and long["fingerprint"] == source,
            "Long clock check failed or source changed")
    require(not long["runtime_mismatches"] and long["trial_error"] is None
            and long["collection_error"] is None, "Long clock recording incomplete or runtime changed")
    require(abs(long["required_duration_s"] - 170.1) < 1e-6
            and long["race"]["reason"] == "deadline"
            and long["race"]["summary"]["elapsed"] >= 170.1 - 1e-6,
            "Full 170.1 second clock check required")
    verify_race(long["race"], long["runtime_info"], engine, "Long clock")
    return {"passes": True, "engine": engine, "clock_mode": CLOCK_MODES[engine],
            "controls": 3, "long_clock_s": long["race"]["summary"]["elapsed"],
            "fingerprint": source, "model_requests": 0}


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--directory", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--engine", choices=tuple(CLOCK_MODES), default="python")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        result = verify(args.directory, args.engine)
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
        print(json.dumps({"passes": False, "error": str(error)}))
        raise SystemExit(1) from error
    print(json.dumps(result, allow_nan=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

@pytest.mark.parametrize("engine", ["python", "rust"])
def test_package_uses_versioned_inputs_without_local_artifacts(fresh_source, tmp_path, engine):
    # Secrets and generated outputs must stay outside the allowlisted archive.
    (fresh_source / ".env").write_text("OPENROUTER_API_KEY=not-a-real-key\n")
    (fresh_source / "src/.env.local").write_text("not-a-real-secret\n")
    generated = fresh_source / "scripts/__pycache__/generated.pyc"
    generated.parent.mkdir()
    generated.write_bytes(b"generated bytecode")
    output = tmp_path / f"{engine}.tar.gz"
    report = packaging.package(fresh_source, output, engine)
    assert report["engine"] == engine
    assert report["expected_clock_mode"] == packaging.CLOCK_MODES[engine]
    assert abs(report["reference_s"] - 56.7) < 1e-6
    assert abs(report["long_clock_s"] - 170.1) < 1e-6

    with tarfile.open(output) as archive:
        contents = {}
        for entry in archive.getmembers():
            assert entry.isfile() and not entry.name.startswith("/")
            name = entry.name.removeprefix(packaging.ARCHIVE_ROOT + "/")
            assert not any(part.startswith(".env") or part in packaging.EXCLUDED_COMPONENTS
                           for part in Path(name).parts)
            contents[name] = archive.extractfile(entry).read()
    manifest = json.loads(contents.pop("PACKAGE-MANIFEST.json"))
    assert manifest["model_requests"] == 0
    assert set(contents) == set(manifest["files"])
    for name, content in contents.items():
        assert hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest() == manifest["files"][name]["sha256"]
    for name, source in packaging.HELPERS.items():
        metadata = manifest["helper_sources"][name]
        assert metadata["source"] == source and not source.startswith("artifacts/")
        assert metadata["source_sha256"] == hashlib.sha256((fresh_source / source).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    for name in ("run_controls.py", "long_clock.py", "environment.py"):
        helper = contents[f"remote-clock/{name}"].decode()
        compile(helper, name, "exec")
        assert f"info.get('engine', 'python') == '{engine}'" in helper
        assert packaging.CLOCK_MODES[engine] in helper
        assert "artifacts/rust-clock-v1/" not in helper


def test_frozen_reference_matches_current_physics_and_original_helper_hashes():

    for name, metadata in provenance["helpers"].items():
        assert hashlib.sha256((directory / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == metadata["sha256"]
    assert hashlib.sha256((directory / "reference.json").read_bytes()).hexdigest() == (

    module = "mcpkart.physics_worker" if engine == "python" else "mcpkart-rust-worker"
    for info in (expected_info, race["runtime_info"]):
        require(info["backend"] == "process" and info.get("engine", "python") == engine,
                f"{label}: wrong engine/backend")
        require(info["clock_mode"] == mode and info["physics_hz"] == 60,
                f"{label}: wrong clock mode/frequency")
        require(info["watchdog_enabled"] is False, f"{label}: watchdog enabled")
        require(info["process_pid"] == expected_info["process_pid"] > 1,
                f"{label}: HTTP parent identity changed")
    provenance, timing = race["process_provenance"], race["timing"]
    require(provenance["worker_module"] == module and provenance["child_clock_mode"] == mode,
            f"{label}: wrong final worker provenance")
    require(provenance["child_web_modules_loaded"] == [], f"{label}: web modules in physics child")
    require(provenance["parent_pid"] == expected_info["process_pid"]
            and provenance["child_pid"] > 1 and provenance["child_pid"] != provenance["parent_pid"],
            f"{label}: physics did not run in a distinct child")
    require(timing["process_provenance"] == provenance, f"{label}: timing provenance mismatch")
    require(timing["clock_mode"] == mode and timing["backend"] == "process"
            and timing["physics_hz"] == 60, f"{label}: wrong final timing clock")
    require(timing["validity_limits_ms"] == LIMITS, f"{label}: timing limits changed")
    require(timing["infrastructure_valid"] and race["realtime_valid"], f"{label}: timing gate failed")
    for key, limit in (("max_lateness_ms", 100), ("p95_lateness_ms", 25), ("drift_ms", 100)):
        require(math.isfinite(timing[key]) and abs(timing[key]) <= limit,
                f"{label}: {key} exceeds timing limit")


def verify(directory: Path, engine: str = "python") -> dict:
    require(engine in CLOCK_MODES, "Unknown engine")
    controls = json.loads((directory / "controls/validation.json").read_text())
    require(controls["passes"] and controls["source_unchanged"] and controls["model_requests"] == 0,
            "Scripted controls did not pass")
    require(len(controls["controls"]) == controls["required_consecutive_controls"] == 3,
            "Exactly three consecutive controls are required")
    require(controls["expected_clock_mode"] == CLOCK_MODES[engine], "Control clock mode changed")
    require(controls["validity_limits_ms"] == LIMITS, "Control timing limits changed")
    source = fingerprint()
    for index, row in enumerate(controls["controls"], 1):
        label = f"Control {index}"
        trial = json.loads((directory / f"controls/run-{index:02d}/scripted-live.json").read_text())
        race = trial["race"]
        require(row["passes"] and row["spectator_polls"] > 0, f"{label}: control gate failed")
        require(trial["fingerprint"] == row["fingerprint"] == source, f"{label}: source changed")
        require(not trial["runtime_mismatches"] and trial["collection_complete"],
                f"{label}: recording incomplete or runtime changed")
        require(race["summary"]["finished"] and race["summary"]["checkpoints_passed"] == 120,
                f"{label}: three-lap race did not finish")
        verify_race(race, controls["runtime_info"], engine, label)
        if index == 2:
            pause = row["parent_pause"]
            require(pause["race_id"] == race["race_id"]
                    and pause["parent_pid"] == controls["runtime_info"]["process_pid"],
                    "Parent pause targeted the wrong race or process")
            require(pause["signals"] == ["SIGSTOP", "SIGCONT"]
                    and abs(pause["requested_duration_s"] - .35) < 1e-6,
                    "Declared parent pause changed")
            samples = [sample for sample in race["samples"]
                       if pause["started_ns"] <= sample["wall_ns"] <= pause["ended_ns"]]
            require(len(samples) == pause["physics_samples_during_parent_pause"] >= 12,
                    "Insufficient actual child samples during parent pause")
    long = json.loads((directory / "long-clock.json").read_text())
    require(long["passes"] and long["model_requests"] == 0 and long["fingerprint"] == source,
            "Long clock check failed or source changed")
    require(not long["runtime_mismatches"] and long["trial_error"] is None
            and long["collection_error"] is None, "Long clock recording incomplete or runtime changed")
    require(abs(long["required_duration_s"] - 170.1) < 1e-6
            and long["race"]["reason"] == "deadline"
            and long["race"]["summary"]["elapsed"] >= 170.1 - 1e-6,
            "Full 170.1 second clock check required")
    verify_race(long["race"], long["runtime_info"], engine, "Long clock")
    return {"passes": True, "engine": engine, "clock_mode": CLOCK_MODES[engine],
            "controls": 3, "long_clock_s": long["race"]["summary"]["elapsed"],
            "fingerprint": source, "model_requests": 0}


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--directory", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--engine", choices=tuple(CLOCK_MODES), default="python")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        result = verify(args.directory, args.engine)
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
        print(json.dumps({"passes": False, "error": str(error)}))
        raise SystemExit(1) from error
    print(json.dumps(result, allow_nan=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
